headline: A tidier checklist
bullets: "Up next" now sits at the top of your checklist, without the empty space above it.
Drafting your checklist says what it did in plain words: the steps are timed back from your date and shaped by what you've decided.

headline: Your checklist and After
bullets: Your checklist leads with the one step that's up next, groups the rest by when they're due, and opens a step right where it sits.
After the day, your plan opens on After, with one clear next step: write the thank-yous. Marking someone thanked only checks them off, and you can undo it.
On an iPad held sideways, the whole question and its answers fit the first screen, even with the "Sign in to save" row showing.

headline: See the full invite
bullets: "See the full invite" opens the whole invite right where you're editing it, in the layout you picked. "Show less" folds it back.

headline: The Day, your vendors, and numbers that agree
bullets: On the day of your event, the board shows only what's due today. The rest of your plan folds away until you want it.
A vendor's page opens in clear groups: who they are, where it stands, how to reach them, the day, money and paperwork.
Counts and money now match on every screen, the budget card is shorter, and the plan for the day is called the day's schedule everywhere.

headline: Sending your invite
bullets: Share & invite now goes in four steps: check your invite page and message, invite your list, share another way, then follow up.
Write and save your invite message, preview it as an email or a text, and see who gets what before anything goes out.
Nothing goes out without your reply link, and a guest you already told is never invited twice.

headline: Guests, your invite page, and bigger screens
bullets: Tap a guest to edit them in one place: their reply, who's coming with them, their +1's meal, and how to reach them.
Your invite page has two layouts and eight color palettes, and it can show your photo.
On iPads and computers, the side menu has Create, Plan, The Day and After, and the top shows your event's name.

headline: Folding, weather and the budget
bullets: Finished groups fold up on their own, and each part of your plan opens its section when you tap it.
Weather works when you give a city and state, like Springfield, VA.
The budget suggestion says where the figure on its button comes from.

headline: Shopping lines
bullets: Combined shopping lines are split, so each item is found and priced on its own.
A store that sells no alcohol no longer prices the bar with mixers or cooking wine.

headline: The board on a computer, and a few loose ends
bullets: On a computer, the board shows the date and your event's name at the top. Double-click the name to rename it.
When the last insurance or vendor-clash item is handled, the board says so and moves on to your next step.
Dietary needs shows how many meals are still unanswered.

headline: Invites and the town ask
bullets: Invites use your own words for the event's name, and the email is signed with the event's host line.
At home, the city is asked once. A ZIP code answers it, and guests see the ZIP wherever the event has one.
When any guest is vegan, the menu has a vegan main, with a note to check the labels on bought items.

headline: A cleaner board on phones and tall iPads
bullets: The phone's menu bar hides only when you scroll down, and the selected tab is underlined.
A tall iPad gets its own board, with no empty band above Where you stand.
Every shopping line has a store search term, and combined lines are split.

headline: Smaller fixes you'll notice
bullets: The day’s schedule opens the doors at your start time, not five minutes after it.
Warnings, like a date that can't work, are easier to spot in dark mode.
The family page shows the dress code, and reply counts say who said yes.

headline: Every price says where it comes from
bullets: Each priced line now says what it rests on: a cited price, your own number, your caterer's quote, or an estimate.
Lines with no price source yet are marked "Estimate — no price source yet," and Your money counts them.
When your plan already costs more than the suggested budget, the budget card leads with your plan's figure.

headline: Food plans follow what you told us
bullets: Picking buffet or trays no longer turns "We'll cook it" into catering.
Caterer steps appear once a caterer is hired, and a booked caterer replaces the grocery list.
Food questions use your event's own place and guest count.

headline: What guests and vendors see matches your plan
bullets: Invites show every day of the event, your name, and one clear place line.
The vendor brief lists dietary counts, your start time, every day, and the full address.
Replies follow your adults-only and no-plus-ones choices.

headline: A warmer light look, and easier reading in both
bullets: Light mode is warm linen with clear panels, and dark mode uses the same panels.
Status colors are easier to read, and small buttons are easier to tap.

headline: The day of, and the days after
bullets: On the day, your plan opens on the day’s schedule: what is up first and what is happening now.
After the date, planning reminders stop, and the money summary says what was spent and who is still owed.

headline: "Nothing needs you" means nothing needs you
bullets: The all-quiet message shows only when no calls are open.
Undo always undoes your most recent change.
Your money compares your budget to what the plan is expected to cost.

headline: New events hear what you typed
bullets: Phrases like "married 25 years" no longer set a date.
A plain "Saturday" means the next Saturday, shown so you can change it.
Occasions you name, like Kwanzaa or a celebration of life, start from their own plan.

headline: Private details stay private
bullets: Your shared invite and family link leave out your notes, money, and who stays where.
Checklist rows open the part of the plan they are about.
